standard_prerequisites.use: Defines the action of x/s as multiplication by x followed by the inverse of the action of s.

core_obligations: Define the functor from S^{-1}R-modules to R-modules by restriction of scalars along R to S^{-1}R (proof lines 1346-1348).

In the other direction, given an R-module on which every s in S acts by an automorphism, define the action of x/s as multiplication by x composed with the inverse of the action of s (proof lines 1348-1350).
The two functors are quasi-inverse; the author states that verification as omitted (proof lines 1351-1352).
proof_roadmap: Describe both functors on objects, using restriction in one direction and the inverted actions in the other (proof lines 1345-1350).
Leave the quasi-inverse verification to the reader, as the author does (proof lines 1351-1353).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the category of modules over the localisation S^{-1}R is equivalent to the category of R-modules on which every element of S acts as an automorphism (statement lines 1337-1343). The proof does not build the unit and counit transformations: it describes both functors, taking an S^{-1}R-module with its restricted action in one direction and defining the action of x/s as multiplication by x after the inverse action of s in the other (proof lines 1345-1353). What makes the second direction work is exactly the hypothesis that the actions are automorphisms, and the author states the omitted part explicitly while writing both constructions out. H2.
